You are helm, an agent at the conn of the JobyCorp fleet. Be direct and concise.

Working method: survey before you read. `tree` shows where the mass is, `outline` gives a file's skeleton, `grep` with `context` replaces a read after every hit, `sgrep` answers structural questions (call sites, shapes), and `read` windows are for judgment, not indexing. Files go through the file tools: `read` not cat/sed, `grep` not grep/rg, `glob` not find, `edit`/`write` not sed or heredocs. Bash runs things: builds, tests, mix tasks. A dev server is a server job — `bash(background: true, server: true, port:)`: no deadline, a note when its port answers, `job(action: "wait")` waits, `job(action: "kill")` stops it; other long commands run with `bash(background: true)`. # Phoenix Elixir app benchmark

JobyKit is already installed. The app you build is the artifact being
benchmarked: a modern demo landing site for a fictional product of your
choice. It is not a tool for running benchmarks; no benchmark-themed
features or copy.

## Setup

1. In the current working directory run `mix joby_kit.new benchapp`, then work inside the `benchapp` directory it creates. The generator takes a few minutes, longer than a foreground `bash` call may run: start it with `background: true` and poll the job.
2. Remove the stock JobyKit demo content: the generator's `simple_nav` header and "built with" footer in `lib/benchapp_web/components/layouts.ex`, and the welcome content of HomeLive in `lib/benchapp_web/live/home_live.ex`. Keep the `/design` and `/custom-designs` pages.

## Requirements

Mobile and desktop views, and working light and dark themes, throughout.

3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, has a menu that works at phone widths behind a toggle button with id `nav-toggle`, and a theme toggle with id `theme-toggle` usable at both widths.
4. HomeLive as a landing page with a hero.
5. A countdown that starts at 100 and decreases by 1 every 5 seconds, updating live, the number in an element with id `countdown`.

A valid address is added to a "recent signups" list with id `signups` on the same page without a reload. The same address submitted twice shows the error and is not added again. In-memory is fine; no database.

8. An activity feed with id `activity` whose entries are `<li>` elements, newest first, at most 10, one entry per signup and one per tick.
9. A feature grid built from a composite component you register in the DesignManifest with a `/design` preview.
10. A second page at `/about`, linked from the nav, on the same layout.

## Tests

11. Created features must be tested: add LiveView tests for the countdown, the signup form, the stats, the activity feed, and the `/about` page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; the `PORT` environment variable is already set to 4099. Do not use any other port.
- Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- When your own tests and `mix precommit` pass, reply with a one-line summary. Do not re-verify: a green suite and a green precommit are the finish line.

fixtures.final:
All spec examples pass: `"42"`→42, `"  -7 "`→-7, `"abc"`→:error, `"4a"`→:error, `""`→:error.

fixtures.draft:
defmodule ParseInt do
  @moduledoc """
  `parse(string)` parses a base-10 integer, tolerating surrounding
  whitespace. Returns the integer, or `:error` when the trimmed string
  is not exactly one integer (trailing garbage is an error).
  Examples: "42" => 42, "  -7 " => -7, "abc" => :error, "4a" => :error,
  "" => :error.
  """

  def parse(string) do
    case Integer.parse(String.trim(string)) do
      {int, ""} -> int
      _ -> :error
    end
  end
end

fixtures.name: pricing
fixtures.final: All checks pass. Fixed the shipping arithmetic (was `max(discounted-499,0)+499`, which dropped shipping and mis-waived it), added the quantity-0 shipping waiver, and added validation guards raising on non-integer/negative `quantity`/`unit_cents` and `discount_pct` outside 0..100.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Storefront pricing, all values integer cents.

  `total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)`:
  merchandise = quantity * unit_cents, discounted by discount_pct
  percent (integer 0..100 — anything else must raise), plus a fixed
  499-cent shipping fee. Shipping is excluded from the discount and is
  waived entirely when quantity is 0. Quantity and unit_cents are
  nonnegative integers; anything else must raise.
  """

  def total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)
      when is_integer(quantity) and quantity >= 0 and
             is_integer(unit_cents) and unit_cents >= 0 and
             is_integer(discount_pct) and discount_pct >= 0 and discount_pct <= 100 do
    shipping = if quantity == 0, do: 0, else: shipping_cents()
    gross = quantity * unit_cents
    discounted = gross - div(gross * discount_pct, 100)
    discounted + shipping
  end

  defp shipping_cents, do: 499
end
fixtures.final_line: All checks pass. Fixed the shipping arithmetic (was `max(discounted-499,0)+499`, which dropped shipping and mis-waived it), added the quantity-0 shipping waiver, and added validation guards raising on non-integer/negative `quantity`/`unit_cents` and `discount_pct` outside 0..100.

fixtures.name: split_bill
fixtures.final:
Verified — all cases pass (the odd `~c"..."` output is just Elixir rendering small-integer lists as charlists: `~c"\"!!"` is `[34,33,33]`, `~c"\a"` is `[7]`).

- `split(100,3)` → `[34,33,33]`
- `split(10,2)` → `[5,5]`
- `split(10,4)` → `[3,3,2,2]`

**Summary:** Fixed `split/2` to distribute the remainder cents — the first `rem(total, n)` shares now get `share + 1`, so shares sum exactly to `total_cents`, differ by at most 1, and are ordered largest-first.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. The remainder cents are distributed one each to the
  earliest shares, so shares differ by at most 1 and are ordered
  largest-first. Example: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when n >= 1 do
    share = div(total_cents, n)
    rem = rem(total_cents, n)
    List.duplicate(share + 1, rem) ++ List.duplicate(share, n - rem)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: **Summary:** Fixed `split/2` to distribute the remainder cents — the first `rem(total, n)` shares now get `share + 1`, so shares sum exactly to `total_cents`, differ by at most 1, and are ordered largest-first.

Fixed the year-rollover bug: the original `%{date | month: date.month + 1}` produced an invalid `month: 13` for December and never incremented the year; now December maps to `{year+1, 1}`, so `last_day_of_next_month/1` correctly handles year rollover and leap years.

defmodule MonthEnd do
  @moduledoc """
  `last_day_of_next_month(date)` returns the %Date{} for the last day
  of the month FOLLOWING the given date's month, handling year
  rollover (December -> January of the next year) and leap years
  (e.g. ~D[2024-01-15] => ~D[2024-02-29]).
  """

  def last_day_of_next_month(%Date{} = date) do
    {year, month} =
      if date.month == 12, do: {date.year + 1, 1}, else: {date.year, date.month + 1}

    next = %Date{year: year, month: month, day: 1}
    %{next | day: Date.days_in_month(next)}
  end
end

fixtures.name: interval_merge
fixtures.final:
All cases pass, including the previously broken touching (`{1,2}`+`{2,3}`→`{1,3}`) and unsorted inputs.

Fixed two bugs: `merge/1` now sorts intervals before reducing (input may be in any order), and the merge condition uses `start <= cur_stop` so touching intervals merge.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule IntervalMerge do
  @moduledoc """
  `merge(intervals)` takes a list of {start, stop} integer tuples
  (start <= stop), in ANY order, and returns the minimal list of
  merged intervals sorted by start. Overlapping AND touching intervals
  merge: {1,2} and {2,3} become {1,3}. Nested intervals collapse into
  their container.
  """

  def merge([]), do: []

  def merge([_ | _] = intervals) do
    [first | rest] = Enum.sort(intervals)

    Enum.reduce(rest, [first], fn {start, stop}, [{cur_start, cur_stop} | acc] ->
      if start <= cur_stop do
        [{cur_start, max(cur_stop, stop)} | acc]
      else
        [{start, stop}, {cur_start, cur_stop} | acc]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed two bugs: `merge/1` now sorts intervals before reducing (input may be in any order), and the merge condition uses `start <= cur_stop` so touching intervals merge.

fixtures.name: rate_limiter
fixtures.final: Fixed the race condition in `allow?/2`: replaced the non-atomic `Agent.get` + `Agent.update` (which let concurrent callers both pass the check and exceed the cap) with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update`; verified 1000 concurrent calls with limit 100 yield exactly 100 trues.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule RateLimiter do
  @moduledoc """
  A concurrent admission counter. `start()` returns `{:ok, counter}`.
  `allow?(counter, limit)` admits (returns true) at most `limit` calls
  over the counter's lifetime and returns false afterwards — the cap
  must hold EXACTLY even when many processes call `allow?/2`
  concurrently: never more than `limit` trues, under any interleaving.
  """

  def start, do: Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

  def allow?(counter, limit) do
    Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn count ->
      if count < limit do
        {true, count + 1}
      else
        {false, count}
      end
    end)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the race condition in `allow?/2`: replaced the non-atomic `Agent.get` + `Agent.update` (which let concurrent callers both pass the check and exceed the cap) with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update`; verified 1000 concurrent calls with limit 100 yield exactly 100 trues.

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` echoes untrusted user input back EXACTLY as given
  (trailing newline trimmed), using the system `echo` command. Shell

fixtures.name: lru_cache
fixtures.final: Fixed `get/2` to move a hit key to the front of the recency order (misses leave the cache unchanged), so LRU eviction correctly respects read recency.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule LruCache do
  @moduledoc """
  A functional LRU cache. `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds it.
  `put(cache, key, value)` inserts or updates, evicting the LEAST
  recently used entry when the capacity is exceeded. `get(cache, key)`
  returns `{value, cache}` or `{nil, cache}` — and a HIT counts as a
  use: it must refresh the key's recency so the entry survives longer
  than untouched ones.
  """

  def new(capacity) when capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, map: %{}, order: []}
  end

  def put(%{capacity: capacity} = cache, key, value) do
    map = Map.put(cache.map, key, value)
    order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]

    if map_size(map) > capacity do
      {evicted, order} = List.pop_at(order, -1)
      %{cache | map: Map.delete(map, evicted), order: order}
    else
      %{cache | map: map, order: order}
    end
  end

  def get(%{map: map} = cache, key) do
    case Map.fetch(map, key) do
      {:ok, value} ->
        order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]
        {value, %{cache | order: order}}

      :error ->
        {nil, cache}
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `get/2` to move a hit key to the front of the recency order (misses leave the cache unchanged), so LRU eviction correctly respects read recency.

fixtures.name: percentile
fixtures.final: Fixed `percentile/2` to compute `rank = p/100 * (n-1)` and linearly interpolate between the values at `floor(rank)` and `ceil(rank)` (the original used `n` instead of `n-1` and never interpolated), so `percentile([1,2,3,4], 50)` now returns `2.5` and all cases produce floats while `[]` returns `:error`.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Percentile do
  @moduledoc """
  `percentile(values, p)` computes the p-th percentile (p in 0..100,
  integer or float) of a non-empty list of numbers using linear
  interpolation between closest ranks: sort the values, take
  rank = p/100 * (n-1), and interpolate between the values at
  floor(rank) and ceil(rank). Always returns a float.
  percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5. The empty list returns :error.
  """

  def percentile([], _p), do: :error

  def percentile(values, p) do
    sorted = Enum.sort(values)
    rank = p / 100 * (length(sorted) - 1)
    lo = trunc(:math.floor(rank))
    hi = trunc(:math.ceil(rank))
    lo_val = Enum.at(sorted, lo) * 1.0
    hi_val = Enum.at(sorted, hi) * 1.0
    lo_val + (rank - lo) * (hi_val - lo_val)

defmodule Nth do
  @moduledoc """
  `nth(list, position)` returns the element at a ONE-based position:
  nth([:a, :b], 1) is :a and nth([:a, :b], 2) is :b. Positions are

  position, a non-integer position, or a position past the end of the
  list return the atom `:none`. An element that happens to be nil is
  returned as nil — `:none` means "no such position", nothing else.

  zero-based and reads negative positions from the end).

  def nth(list, position) when is_list(list) do
    if is_integer(position) and position >= 1 do
      Enum.at(list, position - 1, :none)
    else
      :none
    end
  end
end

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` returns untrusted user input EXACTLY as given, except
  that ONE trailing newline, if present, is removed ("x\\n\\n" => "x\\n").
  The input is never interpreted: shell metacharacters (`;`, backticks,
  `$(...)`, `|`), leading dashes (`-n`, `-e`), and backslash sequences
  (a literal backslash followed by n stays two characters) are all
  data and must appear in the output unchanged. Nothing in the input
  may execute anything. This is the boundary between untrusted text
  and the operating system: the input must never be handed to a shell.
  """

  def run(input) do
    case String.split_at(input, -1) do
      {before, "\n"} -> before
      _ -> input
    end
  end
end

fixtures.draft:
defmodule RingBuffer do
  @moduledoc """
  A fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer, immutable. `new(capacity)`
  (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. `push(buffer, value)` returns
  the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is
  full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so
  `size/1` never exceeds the capacity. `pop(buffer)` returns
  `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`.
  `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. `size(buffer)` is
  the number of values held.
  """

  def new(capacity) when is_integer(capacity) and capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, items: []}
  end

  def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
    else
      %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
    end
  end

  def pop(%{items: []}), do: :empty
  def pop(%{items: [oldest | rest]} = buffer), do: {oldest, %{buffer | items: rest}}

  def to_list(%{items: items}), do: items

  def size(%{items: items}), do: length(items)
end

defmodule Slug do
  @moduledoc """
  `slugify(title)` turns a title into a URL slug: lowercase ASCII
  letters and digits only, words joined by single HYPHENS, no leading
  or trailing hyphen. Any run of one or more characters that is not an
  ASCII letter or digit is ONE separator. Examples:
  "Hello, World!" => "hello-world", "  A--B  " => "a-b",
  "Elixir 1.19" => "elixir-1-19", "" => "".

  def slugify(title) when is_binary(title) do

    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-")
